title: Nuxt Ecosystem
description: Nuxt modules, auto-imports, and the data-fetching composables that make Vue full-stack.

data.text: Nuxt is to Vue what Next.js is to React: file-based routing, server routes, and auto-imported composables on top of a single `nuxt` dependency. Modules extend the framework without you writing build config.
Scaffold and inspect the module registry

data.title: Create a Nuxt project
data.code:
npx nuxi@latest init my-app
cd my-app
npm install
npm run dev

rows: Component library built on Tailwind and Reka UI

data.text: Anything in `components/`, `composables/`, and `utils/` is auto-imported. Server endpoints live in `server/api/` and are ordinary files exporting a handler, so a frontend task and its API can share one repository and one build.

data.caption: pages/products.vue — data fetching with useFetch
server/api/products.get.ts — a server route

data.title: Auto-imports are global by default
data.text: Names in `composables/` and `utils/` leak across the whole app. Keep filenames specific and enable `imports: { autoImport: false }` in heavy projects when explicit imports aid readability.

terms.definition: A package that hooks into Nuxt's build to add routes, components, or config at install time.
Nuxt's implicit import of components, composables, and utils based on folder location.
Composables that fetch data, track pending/error state, and serialise results to the client.
The server engine Nuxt builds on for API routes and deployment presets.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Compare Nuxt with a plain Vue + Vite app: Nuxt adds SSR, file-based routing, auto-imports, and server routes, at the cost of magic and a larger build.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Nuxt wraps Vue with routing, SSR, and server endpoints.
Modules extend Nuxt through configuration, not manual bundler code.
Auto-imports remove boilerplate but hide dependencies.
data.takeaway: Nuxt and Next.js are the same idea for different view libraries — learn one and the other is mostly vocabulary.
